newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil prices drift sideways after deals.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil prices drift sideways after deals.

text.p: The cracked market took a breather on Friday after yesterday's spate of deals that saw 100,000 tonnes of low sulphur sold.
Traders said Thursday's deals had thinned the market, but that it was too early to say its long tone had gone.
"A 50,000 tonne cargo is building in the U.K., ready for an early Jan loading," said one dealer.
Second half January barrels were being looked at nothing sooner.
"Everyone seems to have covered themselves. Don't expect much next week," said one dealer.
A handysize cargo out of Scandinavia was offered at $125 fob NWE, but attracting bids several dollars off this number.
The high sulphur cracked market was quiet with end-users looking relaxed. Dealers said cargoes were available, but were beeing offered discreetly.
"I think prices will have to drop to nearer $100 fob for end-users to get interested," said one dealer. Levels were pegged steady around $107 fob on Friday.
